title: Expose each public published page as discoverable Markus/Markdown
description:
Design-only planning. Source/standards investigation and local documentation
are underway/completing; production behavior, executable acceptance and
benchmarks remain unimplemented. No runtime deployment or rollout authorized.

As an agent or reader visiting a public Papyrus page, I want to discover and
read its current published Markus/Markdown representation, so that I can
consume its content and meaningful structure with less unrelated page markup.

Parent: PPY-29da48cd-8041-4ff0-a154-22afa9b2bc3b.
Dependencies: shared foundation PPY-3f55c3e1-65f6-4fc7-833e-6cecc6a85270 and
post-save behavior PPY-defff04e-17b5-4e28-9bb5-df412601a102.
Related: guide PPY-92de976d-7d0c-40ce-9a3b-2d7de0b6eb7d and RSS/Atom
PPY-33854a5d-da97-4597-9ad2-948a7dd23136.

Acceptance behavior below is **planned, not yet executable or verified**.

```gherkin
Feature: Read each public published page as Markus or Markdown
  Scenario Outline: Discover an alternate from a public page
    Given a current public published <page> in a configured publication
    When a visitor fetches its HTML without running JavaScript
    Then an HTML alternate link and an HTTP Link header identify the same page representation
    And that target returns the declared text/markdown content type with UTF-8 charset
    And its public identity and content match HTML for the same selected published snapshot
    Examples:
      | page                     |
      | homepage                 |
      | editorial article        |
      | ordinary product page    |
      | help or wiki page        |
      | authored listing page    |

  Scenario: Preserve public meaning and layout relationships
    Given a public page with headings, columns, a note, links, citations and media descriptions
    When I read its alternate
    Then I can recover the same claims, qualifications, reading order and public references
    And supported Markus grouping and column relationships are preserved
    And public image alternatives, captions and credits are preserved
    And no substantive content is silently dropped, summarized or invented
    And any unsupported construct is reported as an unresolved serialization or coverage failure
    And the output claims only the syntax supported by the verified renderer contract

  Scenario: Exclude private fields even when present in published storage
    Given published storage also contains internal provenance and whole front matter
    And private policies, prompts, rejected material and editorial notes exist elsewhere
    When its alternate is generated and requested directly
    Then only explicitly allowlisted public page content is serialized
    And no private field, source path, hidden metadata or source-only comment is exposed
    And credentials and private asset references never appear

  Scenario: Preserve the public revision while a newer draft exists
    Given a page has a published revision and a newer private draft
    When the draft is saved or previewed
    Then its public HTML and alternate still represent only the published revision
    And anonymous alternate requests cannot select draft or historical revisions

  Scenario: Keep publication and access boundaries
    Given two publications and an unpublished or access-restricted page
    When an anonymous visitor requests an alternate by a guessed URL or query parameter
    Then the request cannot escape the requested publication's scope or reveal the restricted page
    And absence of a discovery link is not the access-control mechanism
    And errors and headers disclose no private content or metadata

  Scenario: Reflect resolved public includes and listings
    Given a public page contains supported includes or listings
    When public included content changes
    Then both HTML and its alternate refresh from the same eligible published composition
    And only the resolved public content and public relationships are exposed
    And no private selection configuration or unpublished included material is exposed
    And the shared dependency mechanism handles transitive changes and removal

  Scenario: Revise, rename or withdraw a public page
    Given the HTML and alternate have both been cached
    When its public revision, canonical path or public eligibility changes
    Then both representations and their discovery links converge within a documented bound
    And withdrawn alternates and obsolete paths stop serving the removed content within that bound
    And delayed older work cannot restore superseded or withdrawn content
    And failed or pending refreshes are visible and can be retried or reconciled

  Scenario: Keep subscription eligibility independent
    Given a public help page is excluded from RSS and Atom
    When its alternate becomes available
    Then it remains excluded from both feeds
    And its alternate still exists because the page is public and published

  Scenario: Offer accessible content without hidden agent instructions
    Given a public page has an alternate representation
    When either a human or an agent opens it
    Then both receive the same public content without an agent identity requirement
    And no private policy or instruction purporting to override a visiting agent's task is added
    And documentation distinguishes standards-based discovery from optional llms.txt conventions
    And it does not claim that all bots discover or obey those conventions

  Scenario: Document and measure the intended efficiency benefit
    Given a synthetic paired example and a representative public-page corpus
    When an evaluation compares HTML, actual extracted tool input and the alternate
    Then it records payload bytes and token counts with the tokenizer and preprocessing identified
    And it separately checks retained meaning, structure, references and exclusion of private fields
    And cost estimates name the pricing assumptions and account for discovery/retrieval overhead
    And accuracy and latency are measured outcomes rather than promised improvements
    And unmeasured results are explicitly labeled unmeasured
```

Optional later negotiation acceptance, only if same-URL `Accept` delivery is
implemented: verify absent `Accept`, `*/*`, explicit Markdown, weighted HTML
preference, `text/markdown;q=0`, unsupported media ranges, GET/HEAD consistency,
and both CDN fill orders. Preserve existing `Vary` dimensions and include
`Accept` where it selects the representation. Keep explicit alternates as a
discoverable path. No User-Agent detection is necessary.

Narrow implementation sequence: freeze the shared public page projection and
supported syntax; specify serializer behavior and URL mapping; extend existing
projection/page ownership, update/removal/reconciliation and per-page discovery;
verify hosted media types/cache behavior; run fidelity and efficiency evaluation.
Do not create a second publisher, private API or custom site composition system.
Static generated pages, custom projectors and the Pretext route need explicit
coverage before claiming every public page is supported.

Compare parity at the same selected published revision and after the documented
convergence bound; this story does not choose atomic multi-object publication.
Specify whether an alternate serialization failure gates the HTML publication
or blocks feature rollout, preserve the prior valid public revision only while
it remains eligible, and do not advertise an incomplete alternate as faithful.
Public cross-site citations/links remain valid; scope isolation prevents
retrieving another tenant's records by manipulating a request. For supported
code includes, expose only the published expanded snippet, never private
authoring paths, unselected lines or later working-copy contents. Exclude
editorial-only nodes, while preserving literal syntax examples in code fences.

Source findings: `markus_export.py` composes whole front matter with `bodyMarkus`
and emits a build manifest, so it is not a safe public download contract.
`projection/source.py` similarly composes input for rendering. Build-time raw
HTML restrictions do not make all non-rendered source metadata public.
Use inspected Markus syntax; Papyrus image/citation preprocessing is a separate
extension. Includes/listing syntax remains foundation design work.

Local fixture validation used inspected Markus 0.6.0; Papyrus requires
>=0.7.0,<1.0.0. No already-installed supported runtime was found in the bounded
lookup. Validate the fixture and public serializer against the actual supported
renderer before claiming integration acceptance; local grammar validation is
not that evidence.

Primary standards: [HTML alternate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-alternate),
[HTTP Link](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8288.html#section-3),
[text/markdown](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7763.html#section-2),
[Accept/Vary](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-12.5.1),
[cache variation](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html#section-4.1).
The [llms.txt proposal](https://llmstxt.org/) is optional and not an IETF/HTML
interoperability guarantee.

comments.text: Coordination: separate public-page research agent supplied the design; Codex papyrus-monitoring integrated the tracker only after checking eligible claims and current owners. Implementation remains unassigned/open, blocked by the two declared dependencies. README/design artifacts remain local and are not evidence of deployed behavior.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Review corrections integrated: compare the same selected revision after convergence, leaving atomic publication unspecified; define serialization failure gates before rollout; allow normal public cross-site references; expose only selected public code snippets; supported Markus >=0.7,<1.0 acceptance remains pending despite local 0.6.0 fixture validation. Delivery: feature/PPY-3212f1-hn-monitor via draft PR https://github.com/AnthusAI/Papyrus/pull/382 ; not landed in develop, no develop-to-main PR for this change.
